bridgeRouteRisk.summary: BDACS confirms KRW1 has separate deployments on Avalanche, Polygon, BNB Chain, Plume, and Ethereum, but neither issuer material nor the reviewed explorer surfaces disclose a canonical bridge, OFT/endpoint wiring, or each proxy implementation’s mint and burn authority. Every tracked deployment therefore remains an explicitly unresolved route; the aggregate tier matches that worst-route classification.

sources.label: BDACS KRW1 PoC and Avalanche issuance announcement

routes.reviewNote: BDACS identifies Avalanche as KRW1’s initial issuance network. Snowtrace shows a 0-decimal ERC-20 with two zero-address supply creations totaling 10,000,000 KRW1, but the available explorer surface does not establish the implementation, mint/burn controller, or any peer/bridge configuration. It cannot be classified as native issuance or a bridge representation.

sources.label: BDACS KRW1 PoC and Avalanche issuance announcement

routes.reviewNote: BDACS publicly announced a Polygon deployment, but its announcement describes expansion only. No issuer documentation or confirmed explorer-readable implementation identifies whether this address is issuer-minted, bridged, or controlled by OFT or other cross-chain wiring; classification remains unresolved.

BDACS announced the BNB Chain deployment. BscScan identifies the address as KRW1 and exposes only a minimal EIP-1967 proxy runtime; its implementation and authority logic are not verified on the reviewed surface. The proxy alone does not prove issuer-native minting or exclude bridge/OFT wiring.

BDACS lists Ethereum among KRW1’s supported mainnets, but its public material does not disclose this deployment’s implementation, mint/burn authority, source chain, or bridge peer. No canonical or third-party route can be safely assigned.

BDACS announced that KRW1 was added to Plume, but the announcement does not identify whether the supplied address is locally issuer-minted or a bridged representation. The reviewed Plume explorer token page did not expose implementation, mint authority, or bridge/OFT peer data, so the route remains opaque.
